# featureflip_rollout_ramp (Resource)

A rollout ramp: raises a percentage rollout on one targeting rule, or on the default rule, one step at a time on a timer. Creating it starts the ramp, which applies the first step at once and each next step when the previous hold runs out. The flag must be on in the environment. Needs the Team plan or above.

A ramp is not edited: changing `rule_id`, `default_rule`, `steps`, `variation` or `bucket_by` aborts it and starts a new one, whose first step must not be below the rule's current rollout. Refreshing reads its progress (`status`, `current_step_index`, `next_step_at`, `paused_reason`); a finished ramp stays in state and is not restarted. Destroying it aborts a ramp that is still running or paused and leaves the rule at its current percentage, or at `abort_percent`; destroying a finished one changes nothing.

The ramp changes the rule as it goes. If `featureflip_flag_environment` manages the same rule, add its `rollout_percentage` to that resource's `lifecycle.ignore_changes` (for a default-rule ramp, `strategy` and `default_variation`), or the next apply undoes the ramp's progress, and editing the rule by hand pauses the ramp. Deleting the rule ends the ramp, and the next plan starts a new one. Any apply that changes that `featureflip_flag_environment` rewrites every rule, so it pauses a running ramp on the flag; resume it from the app or the MCP server's manage_rollout_ramp.

Import with `<project>/<flag>/<environment>/<ramp-id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "featureflip_flag_environment" "checkout_prod" {
  project     = featureflip_project.web.key
  flag        = featureflip_feature_flag.new_checkout.key
  environment = "production"
  enabled     = true

  rules = [{
    description        = "Logged-in users"
    variation          = "true"
    rollout_percentage = 5
    condition_groups = [{
      operator   = "And"
      conditions = [{ attribute = "logged_in", operator = "Equals", values = ["true"] }]
    }]
  }]

  # The ramp raises this rule's rollout as it goes. Without ignore_changes the
  # next apply would set it back, and editing the rule pauses the ramp.
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [rules[0].rollout_percentage]
  }
}

# 5% for a day, then 25% and 50% for a day each, then everyone.
resource "featureflip_rollout_ramp" "checkout" {
  project     = featureflip_project.web.key
  flag        = featureflip_feature_flag.new_checkout.key
  environment = "production"
  rule_id     = featureflip_flag_environment.checkout_prod.rules[0].id

  steps = [
    { percent = 5, hold_minutes = 1440 },
    { percent = 25, hold_minutes = 1440 },
    { percent = 50, hold_minutes = 1440 },
    { percent = 100, hold_minutes = 0 },
  ]

  # On destroy while the ramp is still running, send everyone back to 0%
  # instead of leaving the rule where the ramp got to.
  abort_percent = 0
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment` (String) Environment key.
- `flag` (String) Flag key.
- `project` (String)
- `steps` (Attributes List) The ladder, 1 to 20 steps. Percentages must rise, the first not below the rule's current rollout. Every hold but the last is 5 minutes to 30 days (43200 minutes). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--steps))

### Optional

- `abort_percent` (Number) Percentage (0-100) to leave the rule at when this resource is destroyed while the ramp is still running or paused. Must not be above the current rollout. Omit to keep the current percentage. Changing it does not touch the ramp. It also applies when a change to the ramp replaces it, before the new ramp starts: with `abort_percent = 0`, editing `steps` drops the rule to 0% first.
- `bucket_by` (String) Default-rule ramps only: the context attribute to bucket by when setting up a new rollout.
- `default_rule` (Boolean) Ramp the default rule instead of a targeting rule. On reaching 100% the ramp makes its variation the default.
- `rule_id` (String) Id of the targeting rule to ramp, e.g. `featureflip_flag_environment.x.rules[0].id`. The rule must serve a percentage rollout. Set exactly one of `rule_id` and `default_rule`.
- `variation` (String) Default-rule ramps only: the variation KEY to ramp to. Needed when the default rule has no rollout yet; otherwise the existing rollout's variation is used.

### Read-Only

- `current_step_index` (Number) Index in `steps` of the last step applied; -1 before the first.
- `id` (String) The ramp id.
- `next_step_at` (String) When the next step applies (RFC 3339), while the ramp is running.
- `paused_detail` (String)
- `paused_reason` (String) Why the ramp paused, e.g. the rule was edited by hand or the flag was turned off.
- `status` (String) Running, Paused, Completed or Aborted.
- `target_variation_id` (String) Default-rule ramps: id of the variation being ramped to.

<a id="nestedatt--steps"></a>
### Nested Schema for `steps`

Required:

- `hold_minutes` (Number) Minutes to hold this step before the next. Not used on the last step; set it to 0 there.
- `percent` (Number) Rollout percentage for this step, 1-100.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with <project>/<flag>/<environment>/<ramp-id>. Importing never
# touches the ramp, even if variation or bucket_by in config differ.
terraform import featureflip_rollout_ramp.checkout web/new-checkout/production/0199a8c4-5b1e-7c2d-9f3a-4e6b8d0c1a2f
```
